tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

# User arbitrations of the blocking report (verbatim, French)

Arbitrages (rapport bloquant, section 7) :

Q1 : (b). Ajouter à §63 « la destination est utilisable dans l'état d'arrivée ».
Q2 : lecture mixte sur l'état d'arrivée : invariants du noyau sur l'état entier, plus ArenaInv de la nouvelle entrée ; NewArenaBase porte cette lecture.
Q3 : réalisation par des pas du noyau. freeSlot (contrat HandlePool v0.5) marque l'entrée libre et incrémente la génération ; préconditions : droit d'administration, pool vivant, handle valide, aucune feuille de l'entrée à Init (Uninit ou Moved), aucune autorité active dérivée d'une compagne de ce pool sur l'entrée ; aucun effet d'endUse. Deux preuves obligatoires :
  (1) témoin complet depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés : newPool, allocSlot, resolve Modify, écriture, transfer de la valeur vers un local de même forme, unresolve, freeSlot accepté ;
  (2) la mise à jour des métadonnées (état libre, génération) est réalisable par une écriture autorisée sous le droit d'administration.
Q4 : garantie par pool : réécrire D.2, D.3 et D.4(3) sur les compagnes du pool du slot ; les pools imbriqués restent permis ; I1 et les garanties du noyau restent prouvées sur l'état entier.
Q5 : la validation du handle précède le contrôle du droit : fail dans les deux cas.
Q6 : réécrire §86 s4 : « La réémission ne modifie ni les octets ni l'état d'initialisation. Une lecture reste soumise aux conditions ordinaires du modèle mémoire, notamment Init, aux droits d'accès et à la validité de représentation pour le type demandé. La Spec 4 déterminera les obligations de construction et de typage des valeurs réémises. »
Q7 : restreindre §78.3 aux ancres du sous-arbre strict de internal qui couvrent une feuille du stockage administré ; prouver que la clause découle de §78.2 et de I3 (lecture Q9), et l'équivalence de reset avec sa séquence du noyau dans les deux sens.
Q8 : ajouter à §47 : le graphe de possession des statiques est acyclique.
Q9 et Q26 : « valide » = active. §69.2 : endUse est rejeté si une autorité détenue par place a un descendant actif détenu ailleurs.
Q10 : (a).
Q11 : (a) fail ; (b) reject ; (c) reject ; (d) mark exige AdminRight ; (e) grow suit le détenteur actuel du bloc ; (f) fail avant le contrôle du droit (contrat DS-v2).
Q12 : avec le nouveau freeSlot, un handle d'entrée libre est périmé : fail.
Q13 : §71.2 inchangé ; préciser au §36 que MetaRight vise la création ou le recyclage d'autorités sur un stockage existant, pas la création d'une allocation fraîche par alloc ; la concurrence entre appels relève de la spec 2.
Q14 : « opérations d'accès » = O9–O11 ; le préciser au §59.
Q15 : restreindre §40 aux emplacements racines utilisables, comme §49.7.
Q16 : définir I5 : toute feuille épinglée appartient à un emplacement utilisable.
Q17 : lecture actuelle.
Q18 : région dont toutes les feuilles sont de taille nulle : base et provenance de l'allocation de l'ancre effective, comme la région vide.
Q19 : H31a : le jumeau à plusieurs pas (conjonct 5) est accepté.
Q20 : non bloquants (classés).
Q21 : pour chaque cas dont le verdict attendu change, conserver le verdict historique, sa justification et le nouveau verdict fondé sur la v0.1 (tableau dans la description de PR) :
  - H21, H50, H51 : nouveau verdict = verdict obtenu ;
  - H49 : conservé comme test de régression, verdict = verdict obtenu, blocage résiduel documenté (décision NoLock) ; exception explicite : le reset rejeté de H49 est dispensé de jumeau positif ;
  - H16 classé spec 3 ; W2 et W3 : les variantes deviennent les cas ; MM2-H H01 : la variante devient le jumeau ; H10 : l'accès sort de l'allocation ; W1 : la valeur est retirée avant freeSlot.
Q22 : non bloquants (frontières ouvertes de la spec) ; exitRoots retenu comme réalisation de référence.
Q23 : lectures dont un témoin du rapport change un verdict :
  - B#1, B#15, B#33, SP-A4, machine S1 et S2 : lectures actuelles conservées (B#15 imposée par Q9) ;
  - B#28 : remplacée par Q9 ;
  - B#45 : remplacée : chaque pin crée une obligation d'épinglage d'identité fraîche ; une feuille est épinglée tant qu'une obligation active la couvre ; unpin désigne une obligation et ne lève qu'elle ; K.ExternalDone porte sur cette obligation ;
  - H-R5 : sans objet ; DS-R1 à DS-R13 : tranchées par Q11, Q27 et Q28.
  Les lectures sans témoin de différence sont conservées.
Q24 : le fournisseur doit être un emplacement utilisable (§71.2).
Q25 : (b).
Q27 : (a).
Q28 : (c) fail (une pile morte invalide ses marques).

Spec : ne pas modifier `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md`. Créer `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md` à partir de la v0, avec les amendements Q1, Q2, Q6, Q7, Q8, Q9/Q26, Q13, Q14, Q15, Q16, Q18, Q24 et B#45 (§74, §75), en anglais ; en-tête : « Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated », suivi de la liste des clauses modifiées. Commit séparé `docs(specs): add memory model v0.1 corrective candidate`. La reconstruction suit la v0.1.
Contrats locaux : HandlePool v0.5 (Q3, Q4, Q5, Q12) et DS-v2 (Q11, Q27, Q28), changements listés dans la description de PR.
Preuves : refaire celles qui sont touchées ; les garanties de Q1, Q3, Q7 et B#45 sont démontrées sur les états atteignables du contrat, sans hypothèse supplémentaire non normative ; tout échec de preuve est rapporté, jamais contourné. Ouvrir la PR si la condition du brief est remplie.

## Follow-up answers (verbatim, French)

Q9 (suite) : règle unifiée. endUse et free sont rejetés si une autorité qu'ils désactivent — détenue par un emplacement qui meurt, stockage possédé transitivement compris, ou racine d'un stockage libéré — a un descendant actif, quelle que soit son empreinte, que le même pas ne désactive pas. Les cas (1) et (2) sont donc rejetés. La sortie de cadre garde son ré-ancrage, et rejette si aucune origine survivante n'existe (inchangé). I2 au sens « origine active » tient après chaque pas.

Q3 (suite) : remplace Q17. Dans §63.4, §69.2 et §70.3, sont exemptées des contrôles « autorité dérivée active couvrant depuis l'extérieur » les autorités par lesquelles le pas exerce son droit Modify : l'autorité exerçable qui fonde le droit et sa chaîne d'origines (pour le pool : entrée, compagne, internal et ses origines). Les autres autorités actives restent contrôlées. Le témoin Q3 (1) devient : resolve Modify, écriture, transfer de l'entrée vers un local, unresolve, freeSlot accepté, y compris avec internal dérivé. W1 suit le même chemin. Réévaluer W2 sous cette lecture. Ajouter §63.4, §69.2 et §70.3 aux amendements de la v0.1.

(Cases (1) and (2) above refer to: (1) endUse(p) where p owns an allocation q holding a stored authority a, the frame holding b derived from a over another static; (2) free(p) with an empty-footprint derivative of p's root held by the frame.)

26	/-- Reading `OptP` with default `True` on a present value (§38). -/
27	private theorem optP_true {α : Type} {o : Option α} {P : α → Prop} {y : α} (h : OptP o P True)
28	    (hy : o = some y) : P y := by
29	  subst hy; exact h
30	
31	/-- `OptP` with default `False` holds on a present value (§38). -/
32	private theorem optP_false_iff {α : Type} {o : Option α} {P : α → Prop} :
33	    OptP o P False ↔ ∃ y, o = some y ∧ P y := by
34	  cases o with
35	  | none => exact ⟨fun h => h.elim, fun ⟨_, h, _⟩ => by cases h⟩
36	  | some y => exact ⟨fun h => ⟨y, rfl, h⟩, fun ⟨_, h, hy⟩ => by cases h; exact hy⟩

38	/-- A frame of the stack is its own ancestor (§39). -/
39	private theorem ancestor_self {F : Frames} {f : Nat} (h : f ∈ F) : ancestor F f f := by
40	  unfold ancestor
41	  induction F with
42	  | nil => cases h
43	  | cons g F ih =>
44	    rw [List.dropWhile_cons]
45	    by_cases e : g = f
46	    · subst e; simp
47	    · have hne : (g != f) = true := by simp [e]
48	      simp only [hne, ↓reduceIte]
49	      rcases List.mem_cons.1 h with rfl | h
50	      · exact absurd rfl e
51	      · exact ih h
52	
53	/-- In a duplicate-free stack `f :: F₀`, a frame of `F₀` does not have `f` as an ancestor (§39,
54	§49.1). -/
55	private theorem not_ancestor_top {f g : Nat} {F₀ : Frames} (hnd : (f :: F₀).Nodup) (hg : g ∈ F₀) :
56	    ¬ ancestor (f :: F₀) f g := by
57	  have hn := List.nodup_cons.1 hnd
58	  have hfg : f ≠ g := fun e => hn.1 (e ▸ hg)
59	  unfold ancestor
60	  simp only [List.dropWhile_cons, show (f != g) = true by simp [hfg], ↓reduceIte]
61	  exact fun h => hn.1 (mem_of_mem_dropWhile h)

68	/-- Owner validity of §49.3 for one place (bounded form). -/
69	private def OwnerOK (s : S3) : Holder → Prop
70	  | .frame f => f < s.nF
71	  | .place o => o < s.P.length

77	/-- The origin chain of an authority covering leaf `l` ends at `z`, a root authority whose
78	footprint is the footprint of a root place containing `l` (§49.6, bounded form). -/
79	private def RootOfLeaf (s : S3) (l : Nat) (z : Authority) : Prop :=
80	  z.origin = none ∧ ∃ r ∈ List.range s.P.length, RootPlace s.P r ∧ partOf s.P l r ∧
81	    (∀ l' ∈ z.footprint, l' ∈ footprint s.P r) ∧ ∀ l' ∈ footprint s.P r, l' ∈ z.footprint

88	private def RootAuthOf (s : S3) (r : Nat) (z : Authority) : Prop :=
89	  z.active = true ∧ z.origin = none ∧ z.mode = .modify ∧
90	    OptP (s.P[r]?) (fun pr => z.holder = pr.owner) False ∧
91	    (∀ l ∈ z.footprint, l ∈ footprint s.P r) ∧ ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P r, l ∈ z.footprint

100	    b ∉ s.ancs a → x.mode = .observe ∧ y.mode = .observe

107	private def PlacesB (s : S3) : Prop :=

109	    OptP (s.P[r]?) (fun pr => r < q ∧ pr.owner = pl.owner ∧ s.dead r = s.dead q) False) True)

131	private def OriginsB (s : S3) : Prop :=

138	private def RootChainB (s : S3) : Prop :=

307	  obtain ⟨l, hl⟩ := exists_mem_footprint hw (s.P.length - r + 1) r (by omega) hr.1

313	    (hn : ¬ OwnedIn s.P src q) : FrameOf (transferEff s src dst) q f := by
314	  induction h with
315	  | @frame q f pl hpl ho =>
316	    exact .frame (pl := pl) (by rw [transfer_P_get, hpl]; simp [ho, heldIn]) ho
317	  | @place q o f pl hpl ho hf ih =>
318	    have h1 : ¬ partOf s.P o src := fun hp => hn (.direct hpl ho hp)
319	    have h2 : ¬ OwnedIn s.P src o := fun ho' => hn (.step hpl ho ho')
320	    exact .place (pl := pl) (by rw [transfer_P_get, hpl]; simp [ho, heldIn, h1]) ho (ih h2)

325	    (hn : ¬ OwnedIn s.P src q) : (transferEff s src dst).Usable q := by

328	    exact .frame (pl := pl) (by rw [transfer_P_get, hpl]; simp [ho, heldIn]) hd ho hf

334	/-- The ownership chain of a place after the transfer (§40, §63 `ok` effect, third item): the
335	former chain if it avoids the storage of `src`; otherwise it goes through the place
336	corresponding to a part of `src`. -/
337	private theorem transfer_frameOf_back {s : S3} {src dst q f : Nat}
338	    (h : FrameOf (transferEff s src dst) q f) :
339	    (FrameOf s q f ∧ ¬ OwnedIn s.P src q) ∨
340	      (OwnedIn s.P src q ∧ ∃ r, partOf s.P r src ∧
341	        FrameOf (transferEff s src dst) ((corr s.P src dst r).getD dst) f) := by
342	  induction h with
343	  | @frame q f pl hpl ho =>
344	    rw [transfer_P_get] at hpl
345	    cases h' : s.P[q]? with
346	    | none => rw [h'] at hpl; cases hpl
347	    | some pl₀ =>
348	      rw [h'] at hpl; simp only [Option.map_some, Option.some.injEq] at hpl; subst hpl
349	      split at ho
350	      · rename_i hh
351	        obtain ⟨r', e⟩ := mvTo_place (dst := dst) hh
352	        simp [e] at ho
353	      · left; refine ⟨.frame h' ho, fun hn => ?_⟩
354	        cases hn with
355	        | direct h1 h2 _ => rw [h'] at h1; cases h1; rw [ho] at h2; cases h2
356	        | step h1 h2 _ => rw [h'] at h1; cases h1; rw [ho] at h2; cases h2
357	  | @place q o f pl hpl ho hf ih =>
358	    rw [transfer_P_get] at hpl
359	    cases h' : s.P[q]? with
360	    | none => rw [h'] at hpl; cases hpl
361	    | some pl₀ =>
362	      rw [h'] at hpl; simp only [Option.map_some, Option.some.injEq] at hpl; subst hpl
363	      split at ho
364	      · rename_i hh
365	        cases hpo : pl₀.owner with
366	        | frame g => rw [hpo] at hh; exact hh.elim
367	        | place r =>
368	          rw [hpo] at hh ho
369	          simp only [mvTo, Holder.place.injEq] at ho
370	          exact .inr ⟨.direct h' hpo hh, r, hh, ho ▸ hf⟩
371	      · rename_i hh
372	        rcases ih with ⟨hf0, hn⟩ | ⟨ho', hd⟩
373	        · left; refine ⟨.place h' ho hf0, fun hq => ?_⟩
374	          cases hq with
375	          | direct h1 h2 h3 =>
376	            rw [h'] at h1; cases h1; rw [ho] at h2; cases h2; exact hh (by rw [ho]; exact h3)
377	          | step h1 h2 h3 => rw [h'] at h1; cases h1; rw [ho] at h2; cases h2; exact hn h3
378	        · exact .inr ⟨.step h' ho ho', hd⟩

380	/-- Places with the same owner are owned through the value at `src` together (§40). -/
381	private theorem ownedIn_of_owner {P : List Place} {src q r : Nat} {pq pr : Place}
382	    (hq : P[q]? = some pq) (hr : P[r]? = some pr) (ho : pr.owner = pq.owner)
383	    (h : OwnedIn P src q) : OwnedIn P src r := by
384	  cases h with
385	  | direct h1 h2 h3 => rw [hq] at h1; cases h1; exact .direct hr (ho.trans h2) h3
386	  | step h1 h2 h3 => rw [hq] at h1; cases h1; exact .step hr (ho.trans h2) h3

398	    cases h' : s.P[q]? with

400	    | some pl₀ =>

402	      split at ho
403	      · rename_i hh
404	        obtain ⟨r', e⟩ := mvTo_place (dst := dst) hh
405	        simp [e] at ho
406	      · cases hq with
407	        | direct h1 h2 _ => rw [h'] at h1; cases h1; rw [ho] at h2; cases h2
408	        | step h1 h2 _ => rw [h'] at h1; cases h1; rw [ho] at h2; cases h2

413	    | none => rw [h'] at hpl; cases hpl
414	    | some pl₀ =>

984	  exact not_ancestor_top (hF ▸ hwf.frames.2.1) hgF hok
985	
986	/-- §63.8 is a local check: its decision depends on the state only through the places and the
987	authorities held within the source, the ones the transfer moves. Two states with the same places
988	and the same such authorities, at the same identities, get the same decision; no global
989	authority-acyclicity check is involved. -/
990	theorem noLocalSelfLock_local {s s' : S3} {src dst : Nat} (hP : s'.P = s.P)
991	    (hA : ∀ (j : Nat) (y : Authority), (s.A[j]? = some y ∨ s'.A[j]? = some y) →
992	      heldIn s.P src y.holder → s'.A[j]? = s.A[j]?) :
993	    NoLocalSelfLock s' src dst ↔ NoLocalSelfLock s src dst := by
994	  have key : ∀ (t t' : S3), t'.P = t.P →
995	      (∀ (j : Nat) (y : Authority), (t.A[j]? = some y ∨ t'.A[j]? = some y) →
996	        heldIn t.P src y.holder → t'.A[j]? = t.A[j]?) →
997	      NoLocalSelfLock t src dst → NoLocalSelfLock t' src dst := by
998	    intro t t' hP hA h j _ hheld hsl
999	    obtain ⟨y, hy, hh⟩ := optP_false_iff.1 hheld
1000	    rw [hP] at hh
1001	    have e := hA j y (.inr hy) hh
1002	    have hy' : t.A[j]? = some y := e.symm.trans hy
1003	    refine h j (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy')) (optP_false_iff.2 ⟨y, hy', hh⟩) ?_
1004	    have ga : (transferEff t' src dst).A[j]? = (transferEff t src dst).A[j]? := by
1005	      rw [transfer_A_get, transfer_A_get, e, hP]
1006	    have gl : holderLeaves (transferEff t' src dst) = holderLeaves (transferEff t src dst) := by
1007	      funext hd
1008	      cases hd with
1009	      | place p => simp only [holderLeaves, transferEff, hP]
1010	      | frame f => rfl
1011	    unfold SelfLock at hsl ⊢
1012	    rw [ga, gl] at hsl
1013	    exact hsl
1014	  refine ⟨key s' s hP.symm (fun j y hy hh => ?_), key s s' hP hA⟩
1015	  rw [hP] at hh
1016	  exact (hA j y hy.symm hh).symm

# ERN — Memory Model Specification v0.1

**Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated**

Modified clauses, relative to v0 (each change is justified by a defect found while formalizing v0):

- §36: `MetaRight` governs authorities over existing storage, not the fresh allocation of `alloc`; §36 and §71.2 contradicted each other.
- §40: `RootHeld` restricted to usable root places, as in §49.7; the two clauses differed on unusable root places.
- §47: the ownership graph of statics is acyclic; a static ownership cycle made §57 false in the initial state.
- §51: a valid origin is an active origin; "valid" was undefined there.
- §57: definition of I5, which v0 named without defining.
- §59: "access operations" are O9–O11; read as all operations, §59 contradicted §69.
- §60.1: a valid origin chain is an active one, read through §44.
- §63.4: the active derived authorities covering the source from outside are named, and the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right are exempt; without this exemption no value could be moved through a derived authority.
- §63.9 (new): the destination is usable in the resulting state; without it an accepted transfer could create an ownership cycle and break §49.8 and §57.
- §69.2 and §70.3: the same exemption as §63.4, and rejection when an authority made inactive by the step keeps an active descendant; without it an accepted step left an active authority with an inactive origin.
- §71.2: the provider is a usable place; v0 did not require it to exist.
- §74 and §75: each `pin` installs an obligation of fresh identity and `unpin` ends one designated obligation; per-leaf pin flags let an `unpin` lift a pin installed by another `pin`.
- §76.6: the reading of the precondition (whole kernel state, `ArenaInv` of the new entry, resulting state); v0 admitted several readings with different verdicts.
- §78.3: restricted to anchors covering a leaf of the administered storage; as written, its second sentence was false.
- §82.2: address and provenance of a pointer to a region whose leaves all have zero physical size; v0 decided no address for that region.
- §86: the last sentence is rewritten; as written, it was false, since `reset` and `issue` leave a recycled leaf `Init` and readable.

**Higher normative authority:** *ERN — Language Charter v0* (October 27, 2026).  
This specification defines the normative rules of ERN's memory model. Technical names (`derive`, `transfer`, `issue`, etc.) designate **abstract semantic operations**; they do not constitute syntax decisions.

## Validation and Revision Procedure

This edition has been validated and acquires normative authority under the ERN Charter v0. Any subsequent semantic change must identify the clauses concerned, justify the change, and preserve the guarantees of the ERN Charter v0. Formal models and proofs are instruments for verifying this specification, not sources of additional rules. Behaviors not determined within its scope are explicitly identified.

## Scope

This specification defines:

- the safe-code contract;
- the abstract machine for allocations, bytes, and accesses;
- the second-class access discipline;
- footprints, authorities, dependencies, frames, and ownership;
- read, write, transfer, release, allocation, and pinning transitions;
- the normative contract of arenas as a reference library abstraction;
- the correspondence obligations between these mechanisms.

It does not define syntax, the complete concurrency model, control-flow conventions, the type system, or compiler lowering. The sequential model's scope does not waive the general guarantees of the Charter.

---

# I. Safe-Behavior Contract

The following contract applies to all safe code and all properly encapsulated abstractions, regardless of their concrete memory representation.

## 1. Definitions of Safe Behavior

**Safe operation:** An operation that imposes no unchecked safety obligation on its user whose violation could compromise the language's guarantees.

**Safe code:** Code that executes only safe operations and does not directly assume obligations specific to unsafe operations.

**Safe interface:** An interface whose every permitted use preserves the language's guarantees when its implementation is correct.

**Safe abstraction:** An abstraction exposing a safe interface; its implementation may use unsafe operations provided it fulfills all their obligations.

content.content:
## 38. Machine State

The access discipline is based on the finite state

\[ S_3=(F,P,I,A,D) \]

where `F` represents the frame stack, `P` the places, `I` their initialization, `A` the authorities, and `D` the validity anchors. Administrative states of arenas and other library abstractions are separate from `S₃`. The external contract `K` is a separate parameter. The internal representation may carry auxiliary information that creates no new rights.

## 39. Execution Frames

`F` is a nonempty stack of identified, non-duplicate frames. Every frame except the initial frame knows its parent. Frames hold temporary authorities and directly local places. The **current frame** is at the top of the stack. `ancestor(f₁, f₂)` means `f₁` is `f₂` or an ancestor of `f₂` in the stack and its call chain.

The base frame, whose identity is 0 in states reachable from the initial state, never exits. An exited frame can neither be the terminal owner of a usable place nor hold an authority that remains active. Frames have semantic existence; no particular runtime representation is required.

## 40. Logical Places, Leaves, and Ownership

A place has an identity, optionally a structural parent, an abstract `kind`, an owner `owner : Frame | Place`, and a logical death marker. Structural parenthood `partOf(p,q)` describes the subplaces of a value; `owner` describes **who keeps the storage** of a root place valid. An owned place may lie outside its owner's direct footprint; ownership and composition are therefore distinct.

A **leaf** is a place with no structural children. `footprint(p)` contains the leaves of `p`, and access rights over a place are evaluated on those leaves. Places transitively owned by a value are not automatically leaves of its `footprint`. A logical unit of the access discipline does not automatically constitute an additional allocation in the elementary memory machine.

A place `p` is **usable** (`Usable(s,p)`) if and only if:

1. `p` exists and is not marked dead;
2. if its owner is a frame, that frame belongs to the stack;
3. if its owner is a place `q`, then `q` is itself usable and the chain terminates at a frame in the stack.

An ownership cycle makes no place usable. `placeFrame(p)` is the terminal frame of this chain when `p` is usable. Structural parts share their parent's owner and death marker. A value may be logically ended by `endUse` without the place that contained it becoming unusable; the substorages it owned may, however, die.

A **root place** has no structural parent. Every **usable** root place has a root authority of own mode `Modify`, with no origin, held exactly by that place's owner (`RootHeld`). This authority cannot be transferred in isolation; root ownership follows a legal transfer of the owning value when necessary.

## 41. Leaf Initialization States

Every tracked leaf has exactly one of the states `Uninit`, `Init`, or `Moved`.

- `Uninit`: no initialized value available in this leaf.
- `Init`: initialized value, subject to type, representation, and storage obligations.
- `Moved`: value consumed by transfer, inaccessible as its former value.

Aggregates may be partially initialized. Both `Uninit` and `Moved` prohibit ordinary reads, while remaining distinct states for diagnostics and end-of-use obligations. An initialization state creates no access permission.

## 42. Authorities, Modes, Holders, and Origins

An authority conceptually has the following fields:

```text
Authority {
    id
    mode: Observe | Modify
    origin?: AuthorityId
    footprint: Set<Leaf>
    holder: Frame | Place
    active: Bool
}
```

`origin` links a derived authority to its current origin. Authorities have fresh identities and well-formed origin chains. A root authority has no origin; a derived authority has one. Creating derived rights does not increase the scope or permitted mode of the origin.

The **holder** (`holder`) is not the **owner** (`owner`). An authority derived by `derive` or `split` is initially held by the current frame; `store` or a permitted transfer may make it held by a place. The derived `issue` operation proceeds through `split` followed by `store`. `release` does not release a root. There is no persistent `Suspended` field: suspension of rights is inferred from active descendants and applies leaf by leaf.

## 43. Effective Rights and Exercise of Authorities

For an authority `a` and a leaf `l`, `effective(s,a,l)` is derived from the active descendants of `a` whose footprint contains `l`:

1. if `a` is inactive or does not cover `l`, its effective mode is absent;
2. if no active descendant covers `l`, the effective mode is the own mode of `a`;
3. if an active descendant with own mode `Modify` covers `l`, the effective mode of `a` is absent;
4. otherwise, when the covering active descendants are `Observe`, the effective mode of `a` on `l` is `Observe`.

The effect is **local to each leaf**: after splitting a region, the origin may retain effective `Modify` over undistributed leaves.

Requested modes are ordered `Observe ≤ Modify`. `ExercisableAt(s,a,m)` means:

- `a` is active and its own mode permits `m`;
- either `a` is held by the current frame;
- or `a` is held by a place `p`, and the current frame has, over **all** leaves of `p`, an authority itself exercisable in mode `m` with sufficient effective mode.

The latter clause is recursive along the holder chain. Thus, being active or covering a leaf does not automatically make an authority exercisable. `HasRight(s,m,p)` means the current frame has exercise in mode `m` and sufficient effective mode **over every leaf in `p`'s footprint**. Every operation requires the modes it actually needs; an authority's own mode alone is insufficient.

## 44. Dependencies and Effective Anchors

`D(p)` is the set of authorities serving as **validity anchors** for place `p`. An anchor is valid as long as the authority it names is active. Dependencies of contained values are accounted for transitively. Relevant dependencies follow the value during transfer; those of its container do not automatically follow a part transferred in isolation.

For an authority `x`, its **effective anchor** is the root reached by traversing its origin chain. It does not necessarily coincide with its current holder. Lifetime constraints are calculated from the frame of that effective anchor and the frames of places that remain usable. A dependency cannot create a right or artificially extend a lifetime.

`AnchorOrder` requires, for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a usable place `q`, that the frame of the effective anchor of `x` be the frame of `q` or one of its ancestors. `AnchorOrderHeld` imposes the same rule on every **active authority held** by `q`. These conditions apply to the resulting states of operations that move or create holder relations.

## 45. Parameters, Returns, and Reanchoring

A call parameter is an **active derived authority held by the caller** before being passed to the callee; its original provenance may go back to an earlier frame. This interpretation does not require that the authority was originally derived in the calling frame; that additional requirement belongs to Spec 3. The caller **yields** the authority to the new frame: it does not simultaneously retain a copy. If the authority remains in that frame upon return, `exitFrame` releases it; **it is not automatically returned to the caller**. To retain its own right, the caller may pass a **fresh derivative** of the authority it wishes to keep: this is ordinary reborrowing. The definition of ergonomic calling conventions is deferred to Spec 3.
# VII. Invariants of Reachable States

Machine states are subject to structural, validity, and exclusivity requirements preserved by permitted transitions under their declared external contracts.

## 49. WF3 — Well-Formedness of Frames, Places, and Authorities

`WF3(s)` is a **predicate on state `s`**. It jointly requires:

1. a nonempty, duplicate-free frame stack, every frame having a valid identity and, except for the base frame, a valid parent; frame-parent relations are well-founded;
2. a place structure whose composition links are valid and **acyclic**; every structural part shares its parent's owner and death marker;
3. valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place;
4. footprints consisting exclusively of leaves of existing places;
5. authorities with valid identities and modes, whose existing origins form **acyclic** chains ending at a root authority;
6. `RootChain`: every origin chain of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root of the **same structural root place** as that leaf;
7. `RootHeld`: every usable root place has its active root `Modify` authority, with no origin, held exactly by its owner;
8. holder validity: every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place.

Numerical ordering of identifiers, parent precedence over child in a list, and bounds on generated identifiers may be used **to represent or prove** this well-formedness in a formalization; they are not normative restrictions on place or authority identities. Preservation of `WF3` by a transition is a **required property of transitions**, not an additional clause of the state predicate. `WF3` does not impose any particular physical object layout: that belongs to refinement into the elementary memory machine.

## 50. I1 — Structural Exclusivity

For two active authorities **unrelated by derivation** covering the same leaf, their own modes must both be `Observe`. This rule also applies to leaves identified as `SharedMutable`; their particular mutation is governed by the `writeShared` contract and creates no exception to I1.

Exclusivity of **effective** modes (`effective_exclusive`) is a consequence of I1 and the definition of `effective`, not the definition of I1. On a leaf, two incompatible authorities cannot simultaneously possess incompatible effective rights. The only permitted independent ordinary coexistence is `Observe` / `Observe`.

## 51. I2 — Conservation of Rights

A derived authority covers only a subfootprint of what its origin chain permits and does not elevate its mode. Derivation and splitting restrictions do not allow duplication of an exclusive right over a leaf. Every active authority is linked to a valid origin according to state and reanchoring rules: an origin is **valid** if and only if it is active, so the origin of an active derived authority is active. Partial suspension follows from `effective`.

## 52. I3 — Validity of Anchors and Dependencies

Every explicit anchor of a still-usable place is valid. An operation cannot invalidate an anchor retained by a place that remains usable. Transitive propagation of dependencies from contained values does not change this obligation. Dependencies are not permissions and are insufficient to justify an access.

## 53. I4 — Consumption and Movement

A `Moved` leaf cannot be read as if it still contained its previous value. Moving a value does not preserve two copies of an exclusive authority. Initialization state and authority-exercise state are separate checks.

## 54. Anchor Ordering and Absence of Orphan Rights

`AnchorOrder` and `AnchorOrderHeld` are defined in Section 44. `NoDangling` prohibits an **active** authority from covering a leaf belonging to an unusable place; the invariant does not say that a leaf is initialized. `NoOrphan` requires every active authority held by a place to be connected to a frame in the stack through a **finite, non-repeating chain** of authorities: the first link is held by a live frame, and each active link **structurally covers the entirety** of the place holding the next link. The link need not have an effective mode over that place. `NoOrphan` guarantees neither the exercisability of all stored authorities nor freedom from blocking.

## 55. ArenaInv — Invariant of the Arena Abstraction

`ArenaInv` is an invariant of the **library contract**, not an additional predicate of kernel state. For every live arena:

- `storage` designates an existing, usable place; the footprint of `internal` is exactly the footprint of `storage`;
- `internal` is active, with own mode `Modify`, held by the arena value;
- available leaves and issued regions belong to the administered storage;
- two still-active issuances have disjoint regions; no leaf of a still-issued region simultaneously belongs to `available`;
- every still-issued block authority is a derivative of `internal` complying with exclusivity and validity rules;
- anchor and ownership restrictions are respected.

Arena entries do not, by themselves, constitute an additional storage owner. Two live arenas may cover common leaves when their `internal` authorities are distinct and their effective rights are compatible; no **global** disjointness of arena footprints is imposed.

## 56. Uniqueness of Live Administration

**An authority identity may serve as `internal` for at most one live administrative abstraction**, whether an arena, `HandlePool`, `DataStack`, or another library administrative instance. Before registering a new abstraction, its creation operation must jointly check the absence of that identity from **all relevant registries of live administrations**. Uniqueness concerns the identity of the `internal` authority, not merely possible overlap of footprints: abstractions with distinct `internal` identities are not forbidden merely because their footprints overlap. Library contracts must make the information required for this guard available to the creation operation; checking only an abstraction's own registry is insufficient.

**This guard is not a condition for any safety property in Section 57.** The effective right (Section 43, case 3) already prohibits a second issuance over leaves covered by an active block derived from the same authority. Rather, the guard preserves the **abstraction contract**: without it, simultaneous administration of the same `internal` could cause `reject` instead of `fail`, or reissue a previously released block that the first administration still considers unavailable. It creates neither permissions nor allocations and introduces no general detection of authority cycles. Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel.

## 57. Main Invariant

\[
Inv3 = I1 \land I2 \land I3 \land I4 \land AnchorOrder \land NoDangling
\]

On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees:

\[
WF3 \land Inv3 \land AnchorOrderHeld \land NoOrphan
\]

`ArenaInv` (Section 55) belongs to the library abstraction: it is not included in this main kernel invariant.

**I5:** every pinned leaf, statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (an active pinning obligation, Section 74), belongs to a usable place.

I5, associated with pinned storage, remains a **specialized obligation** of `K.Pinned`, not a clause automatically implied by sequential accesses alone. This property is required for reachable states under the declared assumptions. Its correspondence with allocations and bytes requires the refinement defined below.

## 63. O4 — Consuming Value Transfer

**Preconditions**

1. `source` and `destination` are usable, and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over their relevant footprints.
2. Source and destination have the **same shape of ordered subtrees**. The `i`-th child of each source part corresponds to the `i`-th child of the corresponding destination part; all nodes are matched. Structural field identity is positional, not an arbitrary matching of children.
3. **All** source leaves are `Init`, and **no** destination leaf is `Init`. The source and destination footprints are disjoint.
4. No exclusive authority is duplicated; validity of derived authorities and active projections is preserved. No active derived authority held outside `source` covers a source leaf, except the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over `source`: the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain. Other active authorities remain subject to this check.
5. **No in-place source leaf is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`). Storage merely **owned** by the source, which is not itself moved by the transfer of that value, does not prevent this transfer.
6. Dependencies of all still-usable places following the value remain valid; non-escape constraints and `AnchorOrder` are checked in the **resulting state**, including transferred anchors of owned places that remain usable.
7. All moved held authorities, including those of owned storage, satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` in the resulting state; no authority may escape a local anchor on the grounds that its containing value was transferred.
8. **Local self-blocking prevention:** For each active authority held before the step by a part `r` of `source` whose holder becomes the corresponding part `corr(r)` of `destination`, that authority's footprint contains **no leaf** of `corr(r)` in the resulting state. Transfer is rejected if this local check fails; no global authority-acyclicity check is imposed.
9. **Destination usability:** `destination` is usable in the resulting state.

**`ok` effect:**

- every source leaf becomes `Moved` and each corresponding destination leaf becomes `Init`;
- every authority held by source part `r` acquires as its new holder the corresponding destination part `corr(r)`, not indiscriminately the destination root;
- places owned by `r` become owned by `corr(r)`; their roots follow this owner according to `RootHeld`;
- value dependencies follow the corresponding places under validity guarantees; no authority is created or duplicated;
- destination places receive the transferred values and rights without automatically moving storage not owned by a source part.

**Other outcome:** `reject`. `transfer` to a call result is subject to these same rules.

A partially initialized structure may be transferred **field by field**, but only for fields individually eligible for transfer. This does not automatically destructure a value that owns storage **at the container level**: that storage stays with the container if the container is not transferred. Conversion between structures with permuted fields must be handled separately, not as a `transfer`.

## 74. O15 — Dynamic Pinning

**Preconditions:** `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over the relevant leaves, and the operation respects applicable pinning obligations.

**`ok` effect:** A dynamic pinning obligation of fresh identity is installed on the relevant leaves. A leaf is dynamically pinned while at least one active pinning obligation covers it. While an obligation is active, `transfer`, `endUse`, `free`, and `exitFrame` are rejected if they act on leaves it pins; removal of this obligation requires `unpin` under `K.ExternalDone`. Pinning does not make contents immutable. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 75. O16 — Removal of Dynamic Pinning

**Preconditions:** `unpin` designates one active dynamic pinning obligation, installed by `pin` on `place`; `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify`, and contract `K.ExternalDone`, applied to that obligation, attests that all relevant external use has ended.

**`ok` effect:** The designated dynamic pinning obligation ends, and only that one: a leaf it covered stays pinned while another active obligation covers it. The step does not itself modify values, their initialization, or their access authorities. Static obligations are not removed by this operation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

**Associated static rule (`StaticPinnedBottom`):** Statics designated by `K.Pinned` must be places **directly** owned by the **base frame**, not merely transitively owned by a static value. This restriction ensures that they do not die when an intermediate frame exits.

# XIV. Arenas and Collective Invalidation — Reference Abstraction

An arena is a **library abstraction**, not a memory-kernel primitive. Operations O17 through O19 are **derived** from operations O1 through O16 and abstraction-specific metadata: `newArena` registers an administration without modifying the kernel; `issue` performs `split` followed by `store` (after checking availability); `reset` performs a `Modify` derivation over all storage—through `derive` or `split`—then `release`, before restoring availability. Their contract below is **normative for the standard-library arena** until Spec 10 takes responsibility for it. It authorizes neither new permissions nor an additional access machine. Arena entries (Section 46) constitute the abstract state of this administration; the guard in Section 56 belongs to its consistency contract. The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here.

/-- After an accepted `transfer` (§63) from a `WF3` state (§49), `NoDangling` (§54) of the
resulting state forces the destination to be usable: an authority of the current frame with
`Modify` over the destination (§63.1) still covers its leaves. -/
theorem transfer_dst_usable_of_noDangling {k : K} {s s' : S3} {src dst : Nat} (hw : WF3 s)
    (h : TransferStep k src dst s (.ok s')) (hnd : NoDangling s') : s'.Usable dst := by
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  refine Decidable.byContradiction fun hu => ?_
  obtain ⟨a, -, -, hall⟩ := hpre.dstRight
  obtain ⟨l, hl⟩ := exists_mem_footprint hw (s.P.length - dst + 1) dst (by omega)
    hpre.dstUsable.lt
  have hal := hall l hl
  cases he : effective s a l with
  | none => rw [he] at hal; exact hal
  | some e =>
    obtain ⟨x, hx, xa, hlx, -⟩ := effective_some he
    have hx' : (transferEff s src dst).A[a]? = some (if heldIn s.P src x.holder then
        { x with holder := mvTo s.P src dst x.holder } else x) := by
      rw [transfer_A_get, hx]; rfl
    exact hnd a _ hx' (by split <;> exact xa) dst hu l (by rw [transfer_footprint]; exact hl)
      (by split <;> exact hlx)

/-- On a state satisfying `KInv` (§57) and `HeldAnchored` (auxiliary, not a clause of §63 nor of
§57), an accepted `transfer` (§63) preserves `KInv` iff its destination is usable in the resulting
state. The destination usable afterwards is not a clause of §63 (`transfer_breaks_kinv`); this
states exactly when §57 holds after the step. -/
theorem transfer_kinv_iff {k : K} {s s' : S3} {src dst : Nat} (hinv : KInv s)
    (hheld : HeldAnchored s) (h : TransferStep k src dst s (.ok s')) :
    KInv s' ↔ s'.Usable dst :=
  ⟨fun hk => transfer_dst_usable_of_noDangling hinv.1 h hk.2.1.2.2,
    transfer_preserves_of_dst_usable_of_heldAnchored hinv hheld h⟩

/-- Every operation, `transfer` included when its destination stays usable (a hypothesis, not a
clause of §63), preserves `KInv` (§57) and `HeldAnchored` (auxiliary) under `DDSound` (§80). -/
theorem op_preserves_of_dst_usable {k : K} {op : KernelOp} {s s' : S3} (hdd : DDSound k)
    (hinv : KInv s) (hheld : HeldAnchored s) (h : op.Step k s (.ok s'))
    (hdu : ∀ src dst, op = .transfer src dst → s'.Usable dst) :
    KInv s' ∧ HeldAnchored s' := by
  have hh' := op_preserves_heldAnchored hinv.1 hheld h
  cases op with
  | transfer src dst => exact ⟨(transfer_kinv_iff hinv hheld h).2 (hdu src dst rfl), hh'⟩
  | _ => exact ⟨op_preserves hdd hinv h fun _ _ e => KernelOp.noConfusion e, hh'⟩
  show (if ((statics[l]?).map (·.2)).getD false then InitSt.init else .uninit) = .init ↔ _
  cases statics[l]? with
  | none => simp
  | some e => cases he : e.2 <;> simp [he]

/-! ## Reachable states (§57) -/

/-- §57 as stated is false: under a contract satisfying `DDSound` (§80) and well-formed statics
(§47), a reachable state violates `KInv`, after an accepted `transfer` (§63,
`transfer_breaks_kinv`). -/
theorem reachable_kinv_false : ¬ ∀ (k : K) (statics : Statics) (s : S3), DDSound k →
    StaticsOK statics → Reachable k statics s → KInv s := by
  intro hall
  obtain ⟨hdd, s, s', hr, -, -, ht, hn⟩ := transfer_breaks_kinv
  exact hn (hall _ _ _ hdd (by decide) (.step hr (.transfer ht)))

/-- A kernel step whose `transfer`, if it is one, leaves its destination usable (§63). The
condition is a hypothesis on runs, not a clause of §63 nor of §57. -/
def KStepDU (k : K) (s s' : S3) : Prop :=
  ∃ op : KernelOp, op.Step k s (.ok s') ∧ ∀ src dst, op = .transfer src dst → s'.Usable dst

/-- States reached from `S3.init statics` by runs whose transfers keep the destination usable
(§57, restricted by the hypothesis of `KStepDU`, which is not a clause of §63). -/
inductive ReachableDU (k : K) (statics : Statics) : S3 → Prop where
  /-- The initial state (§47). -/
  | init : ReachableDU k statics (S3.init statics)

'''

/-- `transfer(1, 4)` from `ahx`''')

content.content:
/-! ## The destination's usability does not suffice (§44, §63.7)

§63.7 checks `AnchorOrderHeld` only for the moved held authorities. In `ahx`, the derived
authority 6 is held by place 2, outside the transferred value, without being among its anchors
(`HeldAnchored` fails), and its effective anchor, the root 3 held by the source, moves with the
value to a younger frame. The state is not built by kernel steps: in such runs a derived
authority is held by a place only through `store` (§65), which also anchors it there. -/

namespace TransferWitness

/-- A state satisfying `KInv ∧ KAux` (§57, §49.7), not reached by kernel steps: frames 1 (current)
and 0; place 0 owned by frame 0; source place 1 owned by place 0, `Init`; place 2 owned by
frame 0; place 3 owned by the source; destination place 4 owned by frame 1. Authorities 0–4 are
the roots of places 0–4; authority 5, derived from 0, gives frame 1 `Modify` on place 0 and,
through it, on the source; authority 6, derived from the root 3, is held by place 2, with no
anchor anywhere. -/
def ahx : S3 where
  F := [1, 0]
  nF := 2
  P := [⟨none, .frame 0, 0⟩, ⟨none, .place 0, 0⟩, ⟨none, .frame 0, 0⟩, ⟨none, .place 1, 0⟩,
    ⟨none, .frame 1, 0⟩]
  I := fun l => if l = 1 then .init else .uninit
  A := [⟨.modify, none, [0], .frame 0, true⟩, ⟨.modify, none, [1], .place 0, true⟩,
    ⟨.modify, none, [2], .frame 0, true⟩, ⟨.modify, none, [3], .place 1, true⟩,
    ⟨.modify, none, [4], .frame 1, true⟩, ⟨.modify, some 0, [0], .frame 1, true⟩,
    ⟨.modify, some 3, [3], .place 2, true⟩]
  D := fun _ => []
  dead := fun _ => false
  pins := []

/-- `transfer(1, 4)` from `ahx` (§63, `ok` effect). -/
def ahx' : S3 := transferEff ahx 1 4

end TransferWitness

open TransferWitness in
/-- With `KInv ∧ KAux` and the destination usable in the resulting state, an accepted transfer
can still break `AnchorOrderHeld` (§44, §54): in `ahx'`, authority 6 is held by place 2 of frame
0 and its effective anchor, the root 3, is now held by the destination in frame 1. `HeldAnchored`
fails in `ahx`. -/
theorem transfer_preserves_of_dst_usable_fails : ∃ s s', KInv s ∧ KAux s ∧ ¬ HeldAnchored s ∧

Spec passages covered (v0.1): §63.1–§63.9 (§63.9 is new), §51 (I2 now requires an active origin), §57 (KInv and I5), §74 (pinning obligations). The module header now names specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md.

Theorems changed:
- `transfer_wf3` (private), Transfer.lean:528: the `hd'` hypothesis is gone; the proof now uses the §63.9 field `hpre.dstUsableAfter`.

- `transfer_preserves_i5`, Transfer.lean:721: `WF3 s → I5 k s → TransferStep k src dst s (.ok s') → I5 k s'`. The pinning obligations, leaves and footprints do not change. `WF3` is needed only to show every usable place stays usable (`transfer_usable_fwd`, using §63.9).

- `cyc2_transfer`: decide proves `TransferPre K0 cyc2 0 3` false, because of §63.9.
